title: A Smile for the Harvest
premise: Bram Lockridge, a rationalist urban explorer, inherits the family farmhouse and discovers tunnels beneath it that appear on no survey—tunnels the founders dug to feed something that keeps the town's harvests alive. When every mirror in the house begins reflecting one second late, Bram realizes the delay is the thing learning their face, preparing to wear them. Refusing to believe even as belief becomes survival, Bram must finish the interrupted founding ritual before the harvest moon rises, aided by cousin Wren, who has spent her life pretending the family was normal. In the end, Bram completes the ritual but learns its price: someone must stay below as the harvest's keeper, and loyalty to Wren forces Bram to choose truth over escape—descending willingly so she can live in the light.
about_author: Coral Lockridge is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent a decade mapping forgotten infrastructure across rural New England before turning to horror. They write about places that remember more than the people who built them.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Bram arrives at the derelict Lockridge farmhouse with surveying equipment and a lawyer's letter they barely read. POV: Bram. The house feels watched, but Bram catalogs the unease as structural settling. Emotional beat: defiant skepticism masking grief over the estranged uncle whose death made them heir.

chapters.title: Tunnels Off the Map
chapters.summary: Exploring the cellar, Bram finds a bricked archway behind shelving and breaks through into hand-cut tunnels absent from every county survey. POV: Bram. The walls are scored with tally marks in generations of handwriting. Emotional beat: explorer's thrill curdling when the tallies count down rather than up.

chapters.title: Wren Knows the Way Down
chapters.summary: Cousin Wren visits, claims she came to help clean, and reacts to the open archway not with surprise but with dread. POV: Wren. She begs Bram to reseal it; Bram refuses. Emotional beat: the fracture between them—Wren's inherited silence versus Bram's need for proof.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Bram notices the hallway mirror lags—a raised hand reflected a beat after the motion. Every reflective surface in the house now does it. POV: Bram. Rational explanations fail one by one through a sleepless night of tests. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in disbelief.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: In the attic, Bram finds the founders' ledger: harvests saved from blight and drought, each entry paired with a name struck through. POV: Bram. The last ritual page is torn out. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not property, but an unpaid debt.

chapters.title: The Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Bram questions neighbors at the fall fair; everyone praises the Lockridges and changes the subject. An old farmer whispers that the reflection isn't late—it's early, showing what comes next. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: isolation deepening as complicity reveals itself everywhere.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren admits her childhood: uncles who vanished 'into the ground work,' a grandmother who never let her look in mirrors after dark. POV: Wren. She shows Bram the torn ritual page she stole years ago. Emotional beat: guilt and relief entwined—the truth finally shared.

chapters.title: The Second Face
chapters.summary: The reflections stop mimicking Bram exactly; the mirrored figure moves independently, smiling when Bram doesn't. POV: Bram. It mouths words Bram can't hear but increasingly understands. Emotional beat: terror of being studied by something wearing your shape.

chapters.title: Below, the Tallies End
chapters.summary: Bram returns to the tunnels and finds fresh tally marks beside their own name. Something has been counting down to them. POV: Bram. A distant rhythmic sound—like chewing—echoes up the shafts. Emotional beat: the moment denial stops being available.

chapters.title: Ritual, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Assembling the ledger, the stolen page, and the founders' tools, Bram reconstructs the rite: a covenant renewed each harvest moon, requiring a keeper below and a witness above. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dawning arithmetic—one of them will have to stay.

chapters.title: Mirrors Go Dark
chapters.summary: Every reflective surface turns black except one: the great hall mirror, where the other Bram waits, patient, offering a trade—step aside and be free. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: temptation rendered intimate; the thing knows exactly how tired Bram is.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises Early
chapters.summary: The moon appears full days ahead of the almanac; the fields outside ripen overnight, impossibly. The town celebrates while Wren panics. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the deadline collapsing, forcing action before either is ready.

chapters.title: Neighbors at the Door
chapters.summary: Townsmen arrive with lanterns and old instructions, insisting the ritual proceed tonight—and that the keeper be chosen by blood lot. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: betrayal; the community's warmth was always bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Lot Falls Wrong
chapters.summary: The drawn token bears Wren's name. Bram protests; the townsmen are gentle, immovable, apologetic. POV: Wren. She accepts with eerie calm, revealing she's expected this since childhood. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Bram Breaks Belief
chapters.summary: Alone in the hall mirror's presence, Bram finally speaks to it—and it answers aloud in Bram's own voice, offering to take Wren's place if Bram surrenders the body entirely. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the skeptic's last wall falling; belief as surrender.

chapters.title: The Descent of Wren
chapters.summary: The town leads Wren to the tunnel mouth singing an old planting hymn. Bram watches, planning, saying nothing. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet courage; Wren has made peace Bram cannot allow.

chapters.title: The Substitution
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Bram shoves past the townsmen and speaks the founder's words first, claiming the keeper's place before the covenant can take Wren. The mirror-Bram laughs—it planned this too. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only honest act left.

chapters.title: What Waits Below
chapters.summary: In the deep chamber, Bram meets the harvest itself: a slow, root-like intelligence fed by kept lives, neither cruel nor kind. It shows Bram the true ledger—all the keepers, all the faces it learned. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: awe stripped of comfort.

chapters.title: The Ritual Finished
chapters.summary: Bram completes the founders' rite from below as the moon crests, sealing the covenant with their own name written last. Above, the mirrors clear; the lag ends. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude fused—the debt paid, the price visible.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: Below, Bram negotiates: the thing wants company and memory. Bram offers stories instead of a second keeper, buying Wren a lifetime. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: survival reframed—not escaping the price, but choosing its terms.

chapters.title: Spring Planting
chapters.summary: Wren remains at the farm as its guardian, telling visitors the Lockridge line ended. Each dawn she leaves a mirror uncovered, and each dawn it reflects on time—except once a year, when it smiles. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: mourning braided with devotion.

chapters.title: A Smile for the Harvest
chapters.summary: Years later, Wren's daughter finds the tunnel entrance open and a lantern burning below, and a voice like an old storybook reading her name kindly. POV: the daughter. Final beat: inheritance continues; the truth waits patiently underground for the next believer.
